Philadelphia Was a Layover

STS-HS11-L2-10001300-HSUSH-PCI-GBL-01 • HS US History and Geography Grade 11 • Ideological Origins of the American Revolution and the Constitution
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Colonists first met the ideas of the American Revolution in books shipped across the ocean from England and France. John Locke wrote that people are born with natural rights, and Montesquieu argued that power should be split so no one person holds it all. On today’s episode of We the Podcast, Tariq interviews Hana about where those ideas came from and where they went next. Within a few decades, people in Haiti and South America were writing declarations of their own.
The Declaration says every person has rights that no government can take away. Why do you think that idea spread to so many other countries?
